title: Inlined Dynamic Virtual Call on Critical Path (Devirtualization Smell)
pattern: Tight loop executing trivial, very short (5-10 instruction) methods via virtual dynamic dispatch (`vtable` or pointer-chasing).
why_bad: Dynamic dispatch prevents compiler inlining, adds branch predictor strain, and incurs function call overhead that can be several times larger than the computation itself.
detection: Dynamic interface or virtual class methods invoked continuously inside innermost loops.
counterexample: The polymorphic handler resolves to highly complex, long-running functions where virtual dispatch is negligible. `Contextual`.
fix: Use monomorphization (C++ templates / Rust generics), devirtualization optimization, or inlining pointers.
